newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says wants top German tax rate under 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says wants top German tax rate under 40 pct.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday he wanted the top rate of German income tax to fall to below 40 percent, from the current 53 percent.
But Waigel, speaking at a tax policy forum of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), declined to be pinned down on exactly what level of income tax top earners should pay.
"Let's give ourselves some room for manoeuvre," Waigel said in answer to a question, confirming a position he stated in Washington during international talks at the weekend.

Germany's Sunday newspapers carried reports of a tax reform plan penned by Kohl's parliamentary lieutenant Wolfgang Schaueble foreseeing a cut in the top tax rate to 35 percent and an entry rate of under 20 percent.
Waigel was said to have approved the document, which will be put to the CDU leadership for approval before going to the annual party conference on October 22.
A broad consensus emerged over the summer on the need to reduce the overall tax burden and simplify a system seen by some as offering loopholes to the wealthy while overburdening ordinary Germans.
But Waigel has resisted pressure from junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to implement a major tax reform before 1999.
